text:
lisa: FYI AcmeCorp (acct_ABC123) reports invoice > dashboard by $12.34 after month close. Invoice total $1,234.56 vs dashboard $1,222.22. Invoice shows charges under 'Standard' but dashboard has Enterprise usage for parts of Feb. Can we repro quickly?

anjali: @lisa can you drop the invoice link and account id? any plan change history? :eyes:

lisa: acct_ABC123 — invoice here: https://invoices.redwood/acct_ABC123/2026-02.pdf. They said they were on Enterprise starting Feb 15 but dashboard shows some days prior still billed at Standard on invoice.

sara: I grabbed consumption rows for Feb. Quick look shows a partition boundary at midnight UTC on Feb 15 where plan attribution flips. Might be timezone + plan-change race where billing window used customer local tz and dashboard uses UTC.

data-andy: Trying a repro query now, posting the SQL I ran:

```sql
SELECT account_id, date_trunc('day', ts AT TIME ZONE 'UTC') AS day, plan_tier, sum(tokens) AS tokens
FROM billing.usage_events
WHERE account_id = 'acct_ABC123'
  AND ts >= '2026-02-01' AND ts < '2026-03-01'
GROUP BY account_id, day, plan_tier
ORDER BY day, plan_tier;
```

data-andy: Results: Feb 14 shows 0 tokens under Enterprise, Feb 15 shows split where some rows are Standard while dashboard groups them under Enterprise. Looks like the plan_change_event at 2026-02-15T00:00:05+01:00 got applied in dashboard logic but billing window used UTC day boundary and assigned earlier few seconds to Standard.

mike: Possible double-count/ retry noise? also check request_id dedupe. If a retry landed across partition and billing backfill ran, could create phantom tokens.

lisa: Customer says they did change plan at 2026-02-15 00:00:03 local time. That aligns with the tiny token delta. They flagged because invoice line recapped rounded totals and the $12.34 shows as extra Standard charges.

anjali: Repro steps I ran: 1) run the SQL above for the account; 2) run delta between billing.usage_events and dashboard.aggregate_usage on the same interval; 3) inspect plan_change_events for midnight boundaries:

```sql
SELECT * FROM billing.plan_change_events
WHERE account_id = 'acct_ABC123' AND occurred_at >= '2026-02-14' AND occurred_at < '2026-02-16'
ORDER BY occurred_at;
```

anjali: That returned a change at 2026-02-15T00:00:03+01:00 — dashboard logic takes local tz for UI grouping, billing pipeline normalizes to UTC cutover when assigning invoice date.

sara: Short-term mitigation: adjust billing pipeline to use account's billing_tz for day-binning OR add a tiny tolerance window for plan changes at midnight so tokens on the same minute are attributed to the newer plan when change_event exists within +/- 10s.

mike: Agree. Also check the invoice generator — rounding can amplify small token shifts. If invoice line grouping collapsed rows, the $12.34 shows up as a Standard line. We should patch rounding to report per-tier subtotals before grouping.

billing-bot: Invoice snapshot generated for acct_ABC123 on 1714780800: total=1234.56, lines=Standard:$45.67; Enterprise:$1188.89

data-andy: Created a short repro gist with query and expected vs actual counts: https://gist.github.com/xyz/repro-acct-ABC123

lisa: Customer asked for credit if we find it's our attribution bug. @mike @anjali can we confirm root cause and ETA for fix?

mike: I'll open BILLENG ticket, assign to eng-billing, priority P2. ETA for a safe mitigation (tz-aware binning fallback) ~ 3 business days to roll a config change, full fix longer.

anjali: For immediate customer-facing response: explain small boundary window, offer $12.34 one-off credit pending root-cause confirmation. I'll hold until we confirm via eng-billing. :+1:

sara: I'll add a unit test in billing pipeline to catch plan_change within 30s of day boundary and assert consistent attribution.

mike: tagging @eng-billing for visibility. Adding the repro SQL and gist to the ticket.

billing-bot: Created issue BILL-2191 (eng-billing) linked to this thread.

lisa: Thanks all — I'll update the customer with the offer and timeline.

mike: small follow-up — can we also check embeds vs generation token split? sometimes dashboard excludes embed tokens from plan-tier counts while invoice includes them. If this account used embedding on Feb 15 that could be another vector.

data-andy: Good call. I'll run:

```sql
SELECT embedding_calls, generation_tokens, sum(tokens) FROM billing.usage_events
WHERE account_id='acct_ABC123' AND date_trunc('day', ts) = '2026-02-15'
GROUP BY embedding_calls, generation_tokens;
```

lisa: Copy. Keep me posted, will wait for BILL-2191 updates. :pray:
